packs.title: Kanji Expansion 1–5: Foundations In Use
packs.description: Thirteen common words unlocked by visible WaniKani kanji from levels 1 through 5, with composition-first meaning stories.

words.meaningMnemonic:
A <kanji>Man</kanji> and a <kanji>Child</kanji> report to the boys' lane, so the category is <vocabulary>boy</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>male</vocabulary>.

男子 is relatively formal and often labels male students, athletes, or categories.
words.readingMnemonic: At the track gate, 男 raises a だん flag and 子 pins on a し badge before every boy runs through. As the last badge clicks into place, the gate calls <reading>だん—し</reading> and admits one <vocabulary>boy</vocabulary>. 男子 is relatively formal and often labels male students, athletes, or categories.

contextSentences.ja: 男子の決勝は午後三時に始まる。
contextSentences.en: The men's final begins at three in the afternoon.

contextSentences.ja: この寮には男子学生が暮らしている。
contextSentences.en: Male students live in this dormitory.

words.meaningMnemonic:
A <kanji>City</kanji> draws a bright wall around everything <kanji>Inside</kanji>; within that wall is <vocabulary>within the city</vocabulary>.

市内 refers to the area inside a particular city's limits.
words.readingMnemonic: A city bus marked 市 hums し while 内 closes the gate with ない and keeps every passenger inside the boundary. The route display blinks <reading>し—ない</reading>, confirming that the bus remains <vocabulary>within the city</vocabulary>. 市内 refers to the area inside a particular city's limits.

contextSentences.ja: 市内のホテルまでバスで行けます。
contextSentences.en: You can take a bus to the hotel in the city.

contextSentences.ja: 大雪のため、市内の学校はすべて休校になった。
contextSentences.en: Because of the heavy snow, every school in the city was closed.

words.meaningMnemonic:
An accountant uses <kanji>Red</kanji> ink for every losing <kanji>Letter</kanji> in the ledger; those red figures mark a <vocabulary>deficit</vocabulary>.

赤字 is used for financial losses or spending beyond income; its opposite is 黒字.
words.readingMnemonic: 赤 spills あか ink across a 字 ledger that stamps じ on every losing line. The red total screams <reading>あか—じ</reading>: the shop has fallen into a <vocabulary>deficit</vocabulary>. 赤字 is used for financial losses or spending beyond income; its opposite is 黒字.

contextSentences.ja: 店は今年も赤字になった。
contextSentences.en: The shop ran a deficit again this year.

contextSentences.ja: 売り上げが伸び、会社はようやく赤字を脱した。
contextSentences.en: Sales grew, and the company finally got out of the red.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Step <kanji>Below</kanji> from the <kanji>Car</kanji> and you <vocabulary>get off</vocabulary> the train, bus, or taxi.

下車する is a formal or written way to say getting out of a vehicle.
words.readingMnemonic: The train floor drops 下 with a voiced げ, then 車 hisses しゃ as the doors open and everyone steps onto the platform. The door chime sounds <reading>げ—しゃ</reading>, and that is your signal to <vocabulary>get off</vocabulary>. 下車する is a formal or written way to say getting out of a vehicle.

contextSentences.ja: 次の駅で下車してください。
contextSentences.en: Please get off at the next station.

contextSentences.ja: 観光客は湖の近くで途中下車し、写真を撮った。
contextSentences.en: The tourists stopped off near the lake and took some photos.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Put the <kanji>Middle</kanji> years of <kanji>Study</kanji> between elementary and high school and you have <vocabulary>junior high school</vocabulary>.

中学 usually refers to junior high school or the junior-high stage of education.
words.readingMnemonic: 中 rings the middle-school bell with ちゅう and 学 answers がく as students rush between two giant school buildings. Both school bells overlap as <reading>ちゅう—がく</reading>, summoning everyone into <vocabulary>junior high school</vocabulary>. 中学 usually refers to junior high school or the junior-high stage of education.

contextSentences.ja: 弟は来年中学に入る。
contextSentences.en: My younger brother will start junior high next year.

contextSentences.ja: 中学ではバスケットボール部に入っていた。
contextSentences.en: I was on the basketball team in junior high school.

words.meaningMnemonic:
When the clock is <kanji>Correct</kanji> at <kanji>Noon</kanji>, both hands point straight up at <vocabulary>midday</vocabulary>.

正午 is exactly twelve noon, not merely the broad lunchtime period.
words.readingMnemonic: 正 straightens the minute hand at しょう while 午 strikes ご and the sun balances directly over the clock. At the instant the hands meet, the clock announces <reading>しょう—ご</reading>: exactly <vocabulary>noon</vocabulary>. 正午 is exactly twelve noon, not merely the broad lunchtime period.

contextSentences.ja: 会議は正午に終わります。
contextSentences.en: The meeting ends at noon.

contextSentences.ja: 正午ちょうどに寺の鐘が鳴った。
contextSentences.en: The temple bell rang at exactly noon.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Take <kanji>Half</kanji> of a <kanji>Year</kanji> and the six calendar pages left are <vocabulary>half a year</vocabulary>.

半年 means a six-month period; はんねん is also an accepted reading in some contexts.
words.readingMnemonic: 半 slices the calendar with はん, and 年 sends とし rolling through the six pages that remain. The six loose pages rustle <reading>はん—とし</reading>, leaving precisely <vocabulary>half a year</vocabulary> on the desk. 半年 means a six-month period; はんねん is also an accepted reading in some contexts.

contextSentences.ja: 日本に来て半年が過ぎた。
contextSentences.en: Half a year has passed since I came to Japan.

contextSentences.ja: 歯の検診を半年ごとに受けている。
contextSentences.en: I get a dental checkup every six months.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Open the official <kanji>Book</kanji> and uncover the registered <kanji>Name</kanji>: the person's <vocabulary>real name</vocabulary>.

本名 contrasts with a nickname, pen name, stage name, or online handle.
words.readingMnemonic: 本 opens with ほん and 名 reveals みょう as a stage mask falls away from the name card. When the mask hits the floor, the card flashes <reading>ほん—みょう</reading> and exposes the actor's <vocabulary>real name</vocabulary>. 本名 contrasts with a nickname, pen name, stage name, or online handle.

contextSentences.ja: この作家は本名を公開していない。
contextSentences.en: This author has not made their real name public.

contextSentences.ja: ホテルの受付では本名を記入してください。
contextSentences.en: Please enter your real name at the hotel reception desk.

words.meaningMnemonic:
A sealed <kanji>Book</kanji> finally speaks its hidden <kanji>Sound</kanji>; what comes out is your <vocabulary>true feelings</vocabulary>.

本音 is what someone genuinely thinks or feels, often contrasted with the public-facing 建前.
words.readingMnemonic: 本 thumps ほん on the table and 音 whispers its kun reading ね from inside the cover. The whisper from the cover grows into <reading>ほん—ね</reading>, finally revealing those <vocabulary>true feelings</vocabulary>. 本音 is what someone genuinely thinks or feels, often contrasted with the public-facing 建前.

contextSentences.ja: 本音を言えば、少し不安です。
contextSentences.en: To tell you my true feelings, I am a little anxious.

contextSentences.ja: 遠慮せずに本音を聞かせてほしい。
contextSentences.en: I want you to tell me what you honestly think without holding back.

words.meaningMnemonic:
A <kanji>Company</kanji> calls a <kanji>Meet</kanji>, and every <kanji>Person</kanji> with a job badge enters as a <vocabulary>working adult</vocabulary>.

社会人 commonly means an adult participating in working society, especially someone no longer a student.
words.readingMnemonic: 社 stamps しゃ, 会 stamps かい, and 人 stamps じん onto a new employee's first business card. The finished card reads <reading>しゃ—かい—じん</reading>, the first official badge of a <vocabulary>working adult</vocabulary>. 社会人 commonly means an adult participating in working society, especially someone no longer a student.

contextSentences.ja: 社会人になって初めて給料をもらった。
contextSentences.en: I received my first salary after becoming a working adult.

contextSentences.ja: 社会人として時間を守るのは基本だ。
contextSentences.en: Punctuality is a basic expectation for working adults.

words.readingMap: しゃ・か・い・じ・ん

words.meaningMnemonic:
Give readers something to <kanji>See</kanji> that <kanji>Exit</kanji> before the body text; it forms a <vocabulary>headline</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>heading</vocabulary>.

見出し labels a newspaper headline, section heading, or dictionary headword.
words.readingMnemonic: 見 shines み through a newspaper while 出し calls its attested chunk だし and pushes the largest line of type above the story. Across the largest type runs <reading>み—だし</reading>, pulling every eye toward the <vocabulary>headline</vocabulary>. 見出し labels a newspaper headline, section heading, or dictionary headword.

contextSentences.ja: 新聞の見出しだけを先に読んだ。
contextSentences.en: I read only the newspaper headlines first.

contextSentences.ja: 各章に分かりやすい見出しを付けた。
contextSentences.en: I gave each chapter a clear heading.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Go <kanji>Outside</kanji> through the <kanji>Exit</kanji> and you are <vocabulary>going out</vocabulary>.

外出する means leaving home or the office for a while, not moving away permanently.
words.readingMnemonic: 外 pulls the front door open with がい and 出 launches しゅつ into the street as shoes leap onto your feet. The door slams out the rhythm <reading>がい—しゅつ</reading> as you step into the street, already <vocabulary>going out</vocabulary>. 外出する means leaving home or the office for a while, not moving away permanently.

contextSentences.ja: 午後は買い物のために外出します。
contextSentences.en: I am going out to shop this afternoon.

contextSentences.ja: 担当者は外出中なので、夕方に戻ります。
contextSentences.en: The person in charge is out and will return this evening.

words.meaningMnemonic:
A <kanji>Small</kanji> grain of <kanji>Wheat</kanji> grows into a field of <vocabulary>wheat</vocabulary> taller than you.

小麦 is wheat; 小麦粉 is the flour made from it.
words.readingMnemonic: 小 shrinks to its kun sound こ while 麦 rustles むぎ across a flour-covered field. The whole field answers <reading>こ—むぎ</reading>, and every stalk bends under the weight of <vocabulary>wheat</vocabulary>. 小麦 is wheat; 小麦粉 is the flour made from it.

contextSentences.ja: このパンは国産の小麦で作られている。
contextSentences.en: This bread is made with domestically grown wheat.

contextSentences.ja: 農家は初夏に小麦を収穫する。
contextSentences.en: Farmers harvest wheat in early summer.

packs.title: Kanji Expansion 6–10: Everyday Organizations
packs.description: Thirteen common words unlocked by visible WaniKani kanji from levels 6 through 10, with composition-first meaning stories.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Plan <kanji>Beforehand</kanji>, then <kanji>Calculate</kanji> every expense; the envelope of planned money becomes a <vocabulary>budget</vocabulary>.

予算 is the amount planned for a project, purchase, household, or government.
words.readingMnemonic: 予 writes よ on every envelope before 算 totals them with さん and locks the cash drawer. When the drawer locks, its display reads <reading>よ—さん</reading>—not one coin may escape the <vocabulary>budget</vocabulary>. 予算 is the amount planned for a project, purchase, household, or government.

contextSentences.ja: 旅行の予算は十万円です。
contextSentences.en: The budget for the trip is 100,000 yen.

contextSentences.ja: 限られた予算内で会場を探さなければならない。
contextSentences.en: We have to find a venue within our limited budget.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Return to your own <kanji>Earth</kanji> at its <kanji>Origin</kanji> and you are back in your <vocabulary>hometown</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>local area</vocabulary>.

地元 can mean one's hometown or the local area around a place being discussed.
words.readingMnemonic: 地 plants a じ sign in the soil while 元 points もと toward the house where the road began. The sign and the old road point together as <reading>じ—もと</reading>, bringing you back to your <vocabulary>local area</vocabulary>. 地元 can mean one's hometown or the local area around a place being discussed.

contextSentences.ja: 地元の野菜を使った料理です。
contextSentences.en: This dish uses locally grown vegetables.

contextSentences.ja: 大学を卒業したら地元に戻るつもりだ。
contextSentences.en: I plan to return to my hometown after graduating from university.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Choose where everyone will <kanji>Meet</kanji>, then mark that <kanji>Location</kanji> as the event <vocabulary>venue</vocabulary>.

会場 is the place where an event, meeting, exam, or performance is held.
words.readingMnemonic: 会 calls かい across an empty hall and 場 answers じょう as chairs unfold for the crowd. Once the chairs finish unfolding, the hall echoes <reading>かい—じょう</reading> and becomes the event <vocabulary>venue</vocabulary>. 会場 is the place where an event, meeting, exam, or performance is held.

contextSentences.ja: 会場は駅から歩いて五分です。
contextSentences.en: The venue is a five-minute walk from the station.

contextSentences.ja: 開演前から会場には長い列ができていた。
contextSentences.en: A long line had formed at the venue before the performance began.

words.meaningMnemonic:
The person who races to <kanji>Write Down</kanji> facts is the <kanji>Someone</kanji> we call a <vocabulary>reporter</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>journalist</vocabulary>.

記者 is a news reporter or journalist, whether working in print, broadcast, or online media.
words.readingMnemonic: 記 scratches き into a notebook while 者 shouts しゃ and lifts a microphone toward the witness. Notebook and microphone snap together with <reading>き—しゃ</reading>, readying the <vocabulary>reporter</vocabulary> for the next question. 記者 is a news reporter or journalist, whether working in print, broadcast, or online media.

contextSentences.ja: 記者が市長に質問した。
contextSentences.en: A reporter asked the mayor a question.

contextSentences.ja: 事件を取材するため、記者が現場に集まった。
contextSentences.en: Reporters gathered at the scene to cover the incident.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Take one organizational <kanji>Part</kanji> and put its <kanji>Long</kanji>-serving leader at the front as the <vocabulary>department head</vocabulary>.

部長 heads a company department and can also head a school club or team.
words.readingMnemonic: 部 rolls a ぶ office chair to the front while 長 stretches ちょう across the biggest nameplate. The enormous nameplate spells <reading>ぶ—ちょう</reading>, so everyone knows where the <vocabulary>department head</vocabulary> sits. 部長 heads a company department and can also head a school club or team.

contextSentences.ja: 部長に企画書を提出した。
contextSentences.en: I submitted the proposal to the department head.

contextSentences.ja: 彼女は今年、吹奏楽部の部長に選ばれた。
contextSentences.en: She was chosen as president of the school band this year.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Take the <kanji>Most</kanji> <kanji>Big</kanji> value the gauge can hold and it reaches the <vocabulary>maximum</vocabulary>.

最大 describes the greatest size, amount, or degree available in the comparison.
words.readingMnemonic: 最 raises a gauge to さい while 大 swells with だい until the needle hits the final mark. The needle crashes against <reading>さい—だい</reading>, unable to climb past the <vocabulary>maximum</vocabulary>. 最大 describes the greatest size, amount, or degree available in the comparison.

contextSentences.ja: この箱には最大で十キロ入る。
contextSentences.en: This box can hold a maximum of ten kilograms.

contextSentences.ja: これは県内最大の図書館です。
contextSentences.en: This is the largest library in the prefecture.

words.meaningMnemonic:
If you can <kanji>See</kanji> all the way <kanji>Pass Through</kanji> fog, you have clear <vocabulary>visibility</vocabulary> and an <vocabulary>outlook</vocabulary> on what lies ahead.

見通し can be a literal line of sight or a forecast about future prospects.
words.readingMnemonic: 見 switches on み headlights and 通し stretches とおし through the fog until the future road appears. The clearing road whispers <reading>み—とおし</reading>, giving the driver an <vocabulary>outlook</vocabulary> on what comes next. 見通し can be a literal line of sight or a forecast about future prospects.

contextSentences.ja: 完成の見通しはまだ立っていない。
contextSentences.en: There is still no clear prospect of completion.

contextSentences.ja: 霧が濃く、道路の見通しが悪い。
contextSentences.en: The fog is thick, and visibility on the road is poor.

words.meaningMnemonic:
At the podium, a sign marked <kanji>Departure</kanji> opens the speaker's mouth; once they <kanji>Say</kanji> the words publicly, the result is a <vocabulary>statement</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>remark</vocabulary>.

発言 refers to something said in a meeting or public setting; 発言する means to speak up.
words.readingMnemonic: 発 fires はつ from the podium and 言 sends げん through every microphone in the room. Every microphone repeats <reading>はつ—げん</reading>, carrying the speaker's <vocabulary>statement</vocabulary> across the chamber. 発言 refers to something said in a meeting or public setting; 発言する means to speak up.

contextSentences.ja: 会議で一度も発言しなかった。
contextSentences.en: I did not speak once during the meeting.

contextSentences.ja: 大臣は誤解を招いた発言を撤回した。
contextSentences.en: The minister withdrew the remark that had caused misunderstanding.

words.meaningMnemonic:
One merchant chooses a crate labeled <kanji>Take</kanji>, while the other uses a rope labeled <kanji>Pull</kanji> to draw it across the counter; their exchange is a <vocabulary>transaction</vocabulary>.

取引 covers commercial dealings, trades, and transactions between parties.
words.readingMnemonic: 取 gathers とり coins and 引 tugs ひき on the contract until both sides shake hands. Coins, contract, and handshake land on <reading>とり—ひき</reading>, completing the <vocabulary>transaction</vocabulary>. 取引 covers commercial dealings, trades, and transactions between parties.

contextSentences.ja: その会社とは長年取引がある。
contextSentences.en: We have done business with that company for many years.

contextSentences.ja: 高額な取引なので、契約条件を慎重に確認した。
contextSentences.en: Because it was a high-value transaction, we checked the contract terms carefully.

words.meaningMnemonic:
A <kanji>City</kanji> turns one <kanji>Location</kanji> into rows of stalls: a bustling <vocabulary>marketplace</vocabulary>.

市場 is read いちば for a physical marketplace; しじょう is used for an economic market.
words.readingMnemonic: 市 calls its kun reading いち and 場 voices ば as stall shutters bang open at dawn. At the first cry of <reading>いち—ば</reading>, every shutter opens and the empty street becomes a <vocabulary>marketplace</vocabulary>. 市場 is read いちば for a physical marketplace; しじょう is used for an economic market.

contextSentences.ja: 朝早く市場で魚を買った。
contextSentences.en: I bought fish at the market early in the morning.

contextSentences.ja: 料理人たちは市場で新鮮な野菜を仕入れる。
contextSentences.en: The chefs buy fresh vegetables at the marketplace.

words.meaningMnemonic:
The main <kanji>Book</kanji> of orders sits in the central <kanji>Part</kanji> of the organization: its <vocabulary>headquarters</vocabulary>.

本部 is the main command center or head office of an organization.
words.readingMnemonic: 本 slams ほん onto the command desk while 部 stamps ぶ on every order leaving the central office. Orders marked <reading>ほん—ぶ</reading> stream from the central desk, revealing the organization's <vocabulary>headquarters</vocabulary>. 本部 is the main command center or head office of an organization.

contextSentences.ja: 災害対策本部を市役所に設置した。
contextSentences.en: A disaster response headquarters was set up at city hall.

contextSentences.ja: 詳しい状況は東京の本部に報告してください。
contextSentences.en: Please report the details of the situation to the Tokyo headquarters.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Gather <kanji>All</kanji> the pieces into one <kanji>Body</kanji> and you can see the <vocabulary>whole</vocabulary>.

全体 refers to an entire object, group, or situation rather than one part.
words.readingMnemonic: 全 calls ぜん and every loose limb flies into 体, which answers たい as one complete body stands up. The reassembled body stands at the call <reading>ぜん—たい</reading>, no longer pieces but one <vocabulary>whole</vocabulary>. 全体 refers to an entire object, group, or situation rather than one part.

contextSentences.ja: まず計画全体を説明します。
contextSentences.en: First I will explain the plan as a whole.

contextSentences.ja: 台風の影響で町全体が停電した。
contextSentences.en: The entire town lost power because of the typhoon.

words.meaningMnemonic:
A <kanji>City</kanji> gathers its <kanji>Peoples</kanji> at town hall; every resident in that crowd is a <vocabulary>citizen</vocabulary>.

市民 means the citizens or residents of a city and often refers to them collectively.
words.readingMnemonic: 市 raises し on a town-hall banner while 民 answers みん from the crowd filling the square. When banner and crowd call <reading>し—みん</reading> together, each resident stands as a <vocabulary>citizen</vocabulary>. 市民 means the citizens or residents of a city and often refers to them collectively.

contextSentences.ja: 市民が公園の計画について話し合った。
contextSentences.en: The citizens discussed the plan for the park.

contextSentences.ja: 市は市民に節水への協力を呼びかけた。
contextSentences.en: The city asked residents to help conserve water.

packs.title: Kanji Expansion 11–15: Plans And Communication
packs.description: Thirteen common words unlocked by visible WaniKani kanji from levels 11 through 15, with composition-first meaning stories.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Mark one specialized <kanji>Part</kanji> of a huge <kanji>Field</kanji> and it becomes a professional <vocabulary>field</vocabulary> or area of study.

分野 is an area of knowledge, activity, industry, or research.
words.readingMnemonic: 分 cuts the research farm into a ぶん plot while 野 marks the gate や for one specialty. The gate marked <reading>ぶん—や</reading> encloses just one research <vocabulary>field</vocabulary>. 分野 is an area of knowledge, activity, industry, or research.

contextSentences.ja: 彼女は医療の分野で働いている。
contextSentences.en: She works in the medical field.

contextSentences.ja: 人工知能は急速に発展している分野だ。
contextSentences.en: Artificial intelligence is a rapidly developing field.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Make two plans <kanji>Suit</kanji> around the same <kanji>Idea</kanji>, and the joined document becomes an <vocabulary>agreement</vocabulary>.

合意 means mutual agreement or consent reached by the parties involved.
words.readingMnemonic: 合 clicks ごう like two puzzle pieces and 意 lights い above both signatures. The two signatures light up under <reading>ごう—い</reading>, sealing the <vocabulary>agreement</vocabulary>. 合意 means mutual agreement or consent reached by the parties involved.

contextSentences.ja: 両社は新しい条件に合意した。
contextSentences.en: The two companies agreed to the new terms.

contextSentences.ja: 話し合いを重ねたが、最終的な合意には至らなかった。
contextSentences.en: Despite repeated discussions, they did not reach a final agreement.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Walk the <kanji>Circumference</kanji> of an <kanji>Area</kanji> and everything around the edge becomes the <vocabulary>surroundings</vocabulary>.

周辺 means the area around a place or the surrounding part of a topic or device.
words.readingMnemonic: 周 rolls しゅう around a map while 辺 plants へん signs throughout the nearby streets. Every nearby street sign points to <reading>しゅう—へん</reading>, mapping the station's <vocabulary>surroundings</vocabulary>. 周辺 means the area around a place or the surrounding part of a topic or device.

contextSentences.ja: 駅周辺には店が多い。
contextSentences.en: There are many shops around the station.

contextSentences.ja: 警察は現場周辺の道路を封鎖した。
contextSentences.en: The police closed the roads around the scene.

words.meaningMnemonic:
Point to what was <kanji>Correct</kanji> at the <kanji>First</kanji> moment of the original plan: what was true <vocabulary>at first</vocabulary>.

当初 refers to the beginning of a period or the original stage of a plan.
words.readingMnemonic: 当 stamps とう on the plan and 初 tears open しょ on its very first page. The first page is stamped <reading>とう—しょ</reading>, showing what the plan said <vocabulary>at first</vocabulary>. 当初 refers to the beginning of a period or the original stage of a plan.

contextSentences.ja: 当初の予定より完成が遅れた。
contextSentences.en: Completion was later than initially planned.

contextSentences.ja: 当初は反対していたが、説明を聞いて考えが変わった。
contextSentences.en: I was opposed at first, but the explanation changed my mind.

words.meaningMnemonic:
A seal marked <kanji>Believe</kanji> stamps one <kanji>Thought</kanji> so deeply into stone that doubt cannot scrape it away; that unshakable mark is a <vocabulary>conviction</vocabulary>.

信念 is a deeply held belief or conviction that guides someone's actions.
words.readingMnemonic: 信 rings しん from a speaker's chest and 念 drives ねん into the promise carved on the wall. The promise on the wall resounds <reading>しん—ねん</reading>, too deeply carved to shake that <vocabulary>belief</vocabulary>. 信念 is a deeply held belief or conviction that guides someone's actions.

contextSentences.ja: 彼は自分の信念を曲げなかった。
contextSentences.en: He did not compromise his convictions.

contextSentences.ja: 医師として患者を第一にするという信念がある。
contextSentences.en: As a doctor, she holds the conviction that patients should come first.

words.meaningMnemonic:
